name: Rob — 110 thermic hours, good cross-country pilot, has never touched collapse work
summary: Well past 100 thermic hours, 20-30km flights are normal, several sites, flies two or three times a month, can name flights his wing cost him. Has never deliberately practised collapses, wingovers or spirals, has never had a collapse, isn't sure he could find the reserve handle quickly, and would rather just get on and fly a new wing.
why_this_persona: The persona the new 'collapse_response_entirely_untested' gate exists for, and the hardest call in this rubric. By hours, currency, cross-country record and honesty about his motives he is a better candidate than several pilots who score higher here. He is capped because the one thing this step's own sources treat as a prerequisite — recovering a collapse with precise, deliberate input — has no evidence behind it from either direction. If the owner decides that gate should be demoted to a Ready-blocker (see meta.owner_decisions in the scoring config), this is the persona whose result flips, and it should flip here and nowhere else.

notes: Computed skills 72.5, psychological 74.2, total 73.3, no bonus. He would be Nearly ready on score alone — his total is below 78 and his skills below the 72 floor is marginal — so the gate is what makes this a Not yet, and the score is still shown alongside it.

EXACTLY ONE GATE fires, which is the point. 'collapse_response_entirely_untested' requires BOTH never having practised and never having handled a real collapse. Two negative checks go with it: a pilot who had practised tip folds themselves would NOT be capped (they would be held at Nearly ready by the collapse_practice Ready-blocker instead), and a pilot who had caught and flown out a real asymmetric would NOT be capped either. Both clearances are deliberate, and the second is why this is not an SIV gate by the back door — he is not capped for lacking a course.

'motivation_reframe_equipment_fix' and 'equipment_as_a_fix_with_thin_readiness' must both stay silent. His motive is 'more glide and speed' and his expectation is 'not a huge difference' — neither is in either trigger. He is not confused about what the wing does; he just hasn't done the work.

'post_collapse_support' must NOT fire. Nothing has gone wrong for him. The suggestion that belongs to him is 'collapse_practice_now', which is about building a skill, not recovering from a fright — and conflating the two would read as implying he's been shaken when he hasn't.
'performance_chasing_reframe' must NOT fire: he can name the flights his wing cost him, so the second half of its trigger is false.

His reserve answer ('I know where the handle is but have never practised') scores exactly 0.5 and passes the Ready-blocker. That is deliberate — see that question's disagreement_note — and 'reserve_practice' still fires, so he is told about it without it holding anything.

TONE CHECK: this is the persona most likely to feel unfairly treated, because everything about his flying is good. The gate message has to carry the whole argument — what the certification wording assumes, why the current wing is the better one to learn on, and that a course is one option among several. Worth reading in full.
